questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An E. coli strain carries a mutation that makes the y gene product completely non-functional; all other lac genes are normal. Lactose is supplied as the only sugar, with no glucose. Which outcome is most likely?
options: The operon is strongly induced, because lactose is present in the medium
Induction is poor, because lactose cannot efficiently enter the cell to inactivate the repressor
The operon is induced, but beta-galactosidase cannot be produced
The repressor is no longer synthesised, so the operon stays on
questions.explanation:
The y gene codes for permease, which increases the cell's permeability to lactose (β-galactosides).
To induce the operon, lactose (as allolactose) must enter the cell and inactivate the repressor.
Without functional permease, very little lactose gets in. The repressor stays bound to the operator, so induction is poor.
Option (1) fails because lactose outside the cell is not enough to induce the operon.
Option (3) fails because the z gene is normal; the problem is lactose entry.
Option (4) fails because the i gene is unaffected, so the repressor is still made.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Proteins cannot serve as genetic material because they fail the very first criterion expected of a genetic material. That criterion is the ability to:
options: undergo slow changes (mutation) needed for evolution
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists the criteria for a genetic material. The first one is that it should be able to generate its own replica (replication).
Nucleic acids can do this because base pairing and complementarity let each strand act as a template.
Proteins have no template mechanism, so they fail this criterion.
Stability (option 1) is a later criterion, and proteins are not ruled out mainly on that basis.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the first phase of translation, amino acids are activated and linked to their cognate tRNAs.
Reason (R): Formation of a peptide bond requires energy, and charged tRNAs placed close together favour peptide bond formation energetically.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: in the first phase of translation, amino acids are activated by ATP and linked to their cognate tRNAs. This is called charging, or aminoacylation, of tRNA.
R is true: forming a peptide bond needs energy. When two charged tRNAs are brought close together, bond formation between them becomes energetically favourable.
R explains A, because charging is done precisely to supply the energy needed for peptide bond formation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which years was the Human Genome Project launched and completed?
questions.explanation:
The Human Genome Project (HGP) was a 13-year project launched in 1990 and completed in 2003.
The year 2006 is a distractor. The sequence of chromosome 1, the last chromosome to be finished, was completed only in May 2006. That does not mark the completion of the HGP itself.
The year 1953 is when Watson and Crick proposed the double helix, which is unrelated.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding DNA fingerprinting is incorrect?
options: Allelic variation at a locus is called DNA polymorphism only if the variant occurs in the population at a frequency less than 0.01
The size of VNTR varies from 0.1 to 20 kb
DNA from blood, hair follicle, saliva and sperm of an individual shows the same degree of polymorphism
Use of PCR has made it possible to perform fingerprinting with DNA from a single cell
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: a variant counts as a DNA polymorphism when it occurs in the population at a frequency greater than 0.01, not less.
(2) Correct: VNTR size varies from 0.1 to 20 kb.
(3) Correct: DNA from blood, hair follicles, saliva and sperm of one person shows the same degree of polymorphism.
(4) Correct: PCR amplifies DNA, so even a single cell can provide enough DNA for fingerprinting.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A double-stranded DNA segment contains 10 adenine–thymine pairs and 15 guanine–cytosine pairs. What is the total number of hydrogen bonds holding the two strands together?
questions.explanation:
Given: 10 A–T pairs and 15 G–C pairs.
Formula: Total H-bonds $= 2 \times (\text{A–T pairs}) + 3 \times (\text{G–C pairs})$, because A pairs with T through 2 hydrogen bonds and G pairs with C through 3.
Substituting: $(10 \times 2) + (15 \times 3) = 20 + 45$
So total hydrogen bonds = 65.
If you swap the bond counts you get 75, which is the trap option.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. In sickle cell anaemia, a single base-pair change in the beta-globin gene replaces glutamate with valine, without any shift in the reading frame.
II. If one base is inserted into a gene and one base is deleted a few codons later, the reading frame downstream of the deletion is restored.
III. Since 61 codons code for only 20 amino acids, every amino acid is specified by more than one codon.
IV. An initiator tRNA recognises the start codon, but no tRNA exists for the stop codons.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
I. Correct: a single base substitution (GAG→GUG) replaces Glu with Val in beta-globin. It is a point mutation, not a frameshift.
II. Correct: a +1 insertion and a later −1 deletion cancel out, so the frame downstream of the deletion is restored.
III. Incorrect: degeneracy applies only to some amino acids. Met (AUG) and Trp (UGG) each have a single codon.
IV. Correct: an initiator tRNA reads AUG, but no tRNA recognises UAA, UAG or UGA.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
The template strand of a short bacterial structural gene reads:
3'-TAC AAG CTT ATT-5'
What polypeptide would be produced on translating the mRNA transcribed from it?
(Codons: AUG = Met, UUC = Phe, GAA = Glu, AAG = Lys, CUU = Leu, AUU = Ile, UAC = Tyr, UAA = stop)
questions.explanation:
The mRNA is complementary and antiparallel to the template strand, with U in place of T.
Template 3'-TAC AAG CTT ATT-5' gives mRNA 5'-AUG UUC GAA UAA-3'.
Reading the codons 5'→3': AUG = Met, UUC = Phe, GAA = Glu, and UAA = stop.
The stop codon ends translation and adds no amino acid, so the polypeptide is Met-Phe-Glu.
Option (2) comes from reading the template strand directly as codons. Option (4) wrongly translates the stop codon.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The secondary structure of tRNA is usually drawn as a clover-leaf. What is the actual three-dimensional shape of a tRNA molecule?
questions.explanation:
The clover-leaf is only the two-dimensional (secondary) drawing of tRNA.
In three dimensions, tRNA folds into a compact inverted L shape. The anticodon loop sits at one end and the amino acid acceptor end sits at the other.
Option (1) is tempting, but it describes the drawn secondary structure, not the real 3-D shape.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the evolution of genetic material is INCORRECT?
options: RNA acted both as a genetic material and as a catalyst in early life
Because RNA was catalytic and reactive, it was unstable, so DNA evolved from RNA through chemical modifications that increased stability
Since RNA can catalyse reactions, it is more stable than DNA and is therefore preferred for long-term storage of genetic information
Being double stranded with a complementary strand, DNA resists changes further by having evolved a process of repair
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: In the RNA world, RNA served both as genetic material and as a catalyst.
(2) Correct: Being reactive, RNA was unstable, and DNA evolved from it through chemical modifications that made it more stable.
(3) Incorrect: Catalytic ability makes RNA reactive and therefore less stable than DNA. DNA, not RNA, is preferred for storing genetic information, while RNA is better for transmitting it.
(4) Correct: Being double stranded, DNA resists change, and it has also evolved repair mechanisms.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the Human Genome Project, the approach that focused on identifying all the genes expressed as RNA is referred to as:
questions.explanation:
The HGP used two methodological approaches.
The first, Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs), identifies all the genes expressed as RNA.
The second, Sequence Annotation, sequences the whole genome, coding and non-coding, and assigns functions to regions later. It is the tempting wrong option, but it does not focus only on expressed genes.
DNA fingerprinting and Southern blotting are techniques, not HGP approaches to gene identification.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Untranslated regions (UTRs) of an mRNA are located:
options: Only at the 5'-end, before the start codon
Only at the 3'-end, after the stop codon
At both the 5'-end (before the start codon) and the 3'-end (after the stop codon)
Between the start codon and the stop codon, interrupting the translational unit
questions.explanation:
NCERT: an mRNA has extra sequences that are not translated. These are the untranslated regions (UTRs).
They are present on both sides of the translational unit: the 5'-UTR lies before the start codon (AUG) and the 3'-UTR lies after the stop codon.
UTRs are not translated, but they are needed for efficient translation.
Options (1) and (2) each name only one end, so they are incomplete. Option (4) describes something like introns, not UTRs.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following non-human model organisms, whose genome has also been sequenced, is a free-living non-pathogenic nematode?
questions.explanation:
Besides the human genome, sequenced model organisms include bacteria, yeast, Caenorhabditis elegans, Drosophila, rice and Arabidopsis.
Caenorhabditis elegans is the free-living, non-pathogenic nematode (roundworm).
Drosophila is an insect (fruit fly), not a nematode.
Arabidopsis is a plant, and Escherichia coli is a bacterium.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the Meselson and Stahl experiment, E. coli fully labelled with $^{15}N$ was grown in $^{14}N$ medium for 80 minutes. The generation time is 20 minutes. What is the ratio of light DNA to hybrid DNA in the population?
questions.explanation:
Given: time in $^{14}N$ = 80 min and generation time = 20 min, so $n = 4$ generations.
Formula: number of molecules = $2^n$. The two parental $^{15}N$ strands always remain in 2 hybrid molecules.
Substituting: $2^4 = 16$ molecules. 2 are hybrid and $16 - 2 = 14$ are light.
So light : hybrid $= 14:2 = 7:1$. The ratio 15 : 1 wrongly assumes only one hybrid molecule remains.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A linear double-stranded B-DNA segment contains 200 base pairs. Adenine makes up 30% of its total nucleotides. Assume Watson-Crick pairing and 0.34 nm per base pair. What are the total number of hydrogen bonds between the two strands and the length of the segment?
questions.explanation:
Given: 200 bp, so 400 nucleotides. A = 30%, so A = T = 120 and G = C = 80.
Pairs: 120 A=T pairs (2 H-bonds each) and 80 G≡C pairs (3 H-bonds each).
H-bonds: $120 \times 2 + 80 \times 3 = 240 + 240 = 480$.
Length: $200 \times 0.34$ nm = 68 nm.
Trap: swapping the pair counts gives $80 \times 2 + 120 \times 3 = 520$.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the ribosome are correct?
(a) It consists of structural RNAs and about 80 different proteins.
(b) In its inactive state it exists as two separate subunits, a large and a small one.
(c) Translation begins when the large subunit encounters an mRNA.
(d) The two sites where successive amino acids bind, so that they come close enough for a peptide bond, are in the small subunit.
(e) The ribosome itself acts as a catalyst for peptide bond formation.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: the ribosome is made of structural RNAs and about 80 different proteins.
(b) Correct: an inactive ribosome exists as separate large and small subunits.
(c) Incorrect: translation begins when the small subunit encounters the mRNA.
(d) Incorrect: the two amino-acid binding sites are in the large subunit.
(e) Correct: the ribosome is itself a catalyst. In bacteria, 23S rRNA is the ribozyme.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In a transcription unit, the promoter lies towards the 5'-end (upstream) of the structural gene, with reference to the polarity of the coding strand.
Statement II: If the positions of the promoter and terminator were interchanged, the strand that acts as the template would also be reversed.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT places the promoter towards the 5'-end (upstream) of the structural gene, with reference to the polarity of the coding strand.
Statement II is correct. The promoter's position fixes which strand is the template (3'→5') and which is the coding strand. If the promoter and terminator were interchanged, these definitions would be reversed, as NCERT states.
So both statements are correct.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The length of the E. coli DNA double helix is 1.36 mm. Taking the distance between two consecutive base pairs as 0.34 nm, the number of base pairs in E. coli DNA is approximately:
questions.explanation:
Given: length = 1.36 mm = $1.36 \times 10^{-3}$ m; distance per bp = 0.34 nm = $0.34 \times 10^{-9}$ m.
Formula: number of bp = total length ÷ distance per bp.
Substituting: $\dfrac{1.36 \times 10^{-3}}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}} = 4 \times 10^6$.
So E. coli DNA has about $4 \times 10^6$ bp. Always convert mm and nm to the same unit first.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a nucleoside, the nitrogenous base is attached to the pentose sugar at which position and by which type of bond?
options: 5' C of the sugar through a phosphoester linkage
1' C of the sugar through an N-glycosidic linkage
3' C of the sugar through a phosphodiester linkage
2' C of the sugar through a hydrogen bond
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): the nitrogenous base links to the OH on the 1' C of the pentose sugar through an N-glycosidic linkage. Base + sugar together form a nucleoside.
Why the others fail:
- A phosphate ester bond at the 5' C turns a nucleoside into a nucleotide (option 1).
- A 3'-5' phosphodiester bond joins one nucleotide to the next (option 3).
- Hydrogen bonds join bases on opposite strands, not a base to its sugar (option 4).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Each of the following changes occurs within the coding region of a structural gene. How many of them will change the reading frame from the point of mutation onwards?
(i) Insertion of one base
(ii) Deletion of two bases
(iii) Insertion of three bases
(iv) Deletion of six bases
(v) Insertion of four bases
(vi) Substitution of one base by another
questions.explanation:
Rule: an insertion or deletion shifts the reading frame only if the number of bases is not a multiple of 3.
(i) +1 base: frameshift.
(ii) −2 bases: frameshift.
(iii) +3 bases: adds one codon, so the frame is kept.
(iv) −6 bases: removes two codons, so the frame is kept.
(v) +4 bases: frameshift.
(vi) Substitution: alters one codon only, so no frameshift.
That gives 3 frameshifts.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following nitrogenous bases are pyrimidines?
Adenine, Cytosine, Guanine, Uracil, Thymine
questions.explanation:
Classify each base:
- Adenine: purine (two rings).
- Guanine: purine.
- Cytosine: pyrimidine (one ring); found in both DNA and RNA.
- Uracil: pyrimidine; found in RNA.
- Thymine: pyrimidine; found in DNA.
So three of the five bases (C, U, T) are pyrimidines.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell, which RNA polymerase transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs?
options: The single RNA polymerase found in mitochondria
questions.explanation:
Eukaryotic nuclei have three RNA polymerases:
- RNA pol I makes the 28S, 18S and 5.8S rRNAs.
- RNA pol II makes hnRNA, the precursor of mRNA.
- RNA pol III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.
The tempting option is pol I, because 5S is an rRNA. However, 5S rRNA is specifically transcribed by pol III.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about DNA packaging in eukaryotes are correct?
(a) Histones acquire their positive charge from lysine and arginine residues in their side chains.
(b) The beads-on-string appearance of chromatin is observed under a light microscope.
(c) Packaging of chromatin at a higher level requires non-histone chromosomal proteins.
(d) Chromatin fibres are further coiled and condensed at metaphase to form chromosomes.
(e) Heterochromatin stains light and is transcriptionally active.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: lysine and arginine are basic residues, so histones are positively charged.
(b) Incorrect: the beads-on-string structure is seen only under the electron microscope.
(c) Correct: higher-level packaging needs non-histone chromosomal (NHC) proteins.
(d) Correct: chromatin fibres coil and condense further at metaphase to form chromosomes.
(e) Incorrect: heterochromatin is densely packed, stains dark and is inactive. Euchromatin is the light-staining, active form.
Three statements, (a), (c) and (d), are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the central dogma proposed by Francis Crick, genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein. In some viruses, information flows in the reverse direction, from RNA to DNA. This reverse process is called:
questions.explanation:
The central dogma describes information flow as DNA → RNA (transcription) → protein (translation).
In some viruses, such as retroviruses, the enzyme reverse transcriptase makes DNA from an RNA template.
This reverses the transcription step, so it is called reverse transcription.
Translation is RNA → protein, and replication is DNA → DNA.
Transformation is the uptake of foreign DNA by a cell.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the Meselson and Stahl experiment, how was DNA containing $^{15}N$ distinguished from DNA containing $^{14}N$?
options: By centrifugation in a caesium chloride (CsCl) density gradient
By separating the DNA according to its charge using gel electrophoresis
questions.explanation:
$^{15}N$ is a heavy isotope but it is not radioactive.
DNA containing $^{15}N$ is therefore denser than $^{14}N$ DNA.
In a CsCl density gradient, each DNA settles at the band matching its own density. Heavy, hybrid and light DNA thus form separate bands.
Options (1) and (3) fail because $^{15}N$ emits no radiation to detect.
Option (4) fails because both DNAs carry the same charge per nucleotide.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to the salient features of the human genome.
List-I
A. Dystrophin
B. Chromosome 1
C. Y chromosome
D. SNPs
List-II
I. Has the fewest genes, 231
II. About 1.4 million locations of single-base differences
III. Largest known human gene, 2.4 million bases
IV. Has the most genes, 2968
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. Dystrophin is the largest known human gene (2.4 million bases) → III.
B. Chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968) → IV.
C. The Y chromosome has the fewest genes (231) → I.
D. About 1.4 million SNP locations were identified → II.
Option (2) is the trap: it confuses the largest gene with the chromosome that has the most genes.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place during the S-phase of the cell cycle.
Statement II: If cell division fails after DNA replication, polyploidy can result.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: In eukaryotes, DNA replication occurs in the S-phase of the cell cycle.
Statement II is correct: Replication must be coordinated with cell division. If the replicated DNA is not divided between daughter cells, the chromosome sets double, giving polyploidy (a chromosomal anomaly).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) The 2'-OH group present in every RNA nucleotide makes RNA reactive and easily degradable.
(b) The presence of thymine in place of uracil gives DNA additional stability.
(c) Viruses with an RNA genome mutate and evolve faster.
(d) DNA can directly code for the synthesis of proteins without RNA.
(e) Proteins satisfy the criterion of being able to generate their own replica.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: the 2'-OH group makes RNA labile and easily degradable.
(b) Correct: having thymine (5-methyl uracil) instead of uracil gives DNA extra stability.
(c) Correct: RNA is less stable, so RNA viruses mutate and evolve faster.
(d) Incorrect: DNA depends on RNA (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA) for protein synthesis.
(e) Incorrect: proteins cannot replicate themselves, so they fail the first criterion for genetic material.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. DNA ligase
B. Origin of replication
C. Taylor and colleagues
D. Meselson and Stahl
List-II
I. Radioactive thymidine in Vicia faba chromosomes
II. $^{15}NH_4Cl$ and CsCl gradient in E. coli
III. Joins discontinuously synthesised fragments
IV. Provided by vectors in recombinant DNA procedures
questions.explanation:
A–III: DNA ligase seals the discontinuously synthesised fragments.
B–IV: A cloned DNA piece cannot replicate on its own, so the vector provides the origin of replication.
C–I: Taylor and colleagues used radioactive thymidine in Vicia faba chromosomes to show semiconservative replication.
D–II: Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in $^{15}NH_4Cl$ and separated the DNA by CsCl density gradient centrifugation.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A double-stranded DNA segment is 200 bp long, and 30% of its total bases are adenine. How many hydrogen bonds hold its two strands together?
questions.explanation:
Given: 200 bp = 400 bases, and A = 30% of all bases.
A = 30% of 400 = 120, and T = 120. So there are 120 A–T pairs.
G–C pairs = $200 - 120 = 80$.
H-bonds: each A–T pair has 2 and each G–C pair has 3.
Total = $120\times2 + 80\times3 = 240 + 240 = 480$.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the Watson–Crick double helix model of DNA are correct?
1. The two strands are coiled in a right-handed fashion.
2. The pitch of the helix is 3.4 nm.
3. There are roughly 10 bp in each turn.
4. Both strands run with the same 5' to 3' polarity.
5. The sugar-phosphate backbone lies outside, and the bases project inside.
6. Stacking of base-pair planes adds to the stability given by H-bonds.
questions.explanation:
1. Correct: the double helix is right-handed.
2. Correct: the pitch is 3.4 nm.
3. Correct: there are about 10 bp per turn, about 0.34 nm apart.
4. Incorrect: the strands are antiparallel. One runs 5'→3' and the other runs 3'→5'.
5. Correct: the sugar-phosphate backbone is on the outside and the bases point inward.
6. Correct: stacking of the base-pair planes adds stability on top of the H-bonds.
So 5 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the lac operon, the regulatory gene is called the 'i' gene. The letter 'i' is derived from the word:
questions.explanation:
NCERT notes that the 'i' in the i gene does not stand for inducer. It comes from 'inhibitor'.
The i gene codes for the repressor, which inhibits transcription of the lac operon.
The tempting option, 'inducer', is wrong. The inducer is lactose or allolactose, a molecule that inactivates the repressor. It is not the gene itself.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Griffith's experiments, some colonies of Streptococcus pneumoniae on a culture plate looked smooth and shiny. What is the reason for this appearance?
options: The cells lack a cell wall
The cells have a mucous polysaccharide coat
The cells contain plasmids carrying virulence genes
The cells have been killed by heat
questions.explanation:
S strain Streptococcus pneumoniae cells have a mucous (polysaccharide) coat. This coat makes their colonies smooth and shiny and makes the strain virulent.
R strain cells lack this coat, so they form rough colonies and are non-virulent.
Bacterial cells do have cell walls, so option (1) is wrong. Plasmids do not explain how a colony looks. Heat-killed cells do not form colonies at all.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An E. coli mutant has a deleted i gene, so no functional repressor is made. It is grown in a medium with glycerol as the carbon source and no lactose. What is the expected status of the lac structural genes (z, y, a)?
options: Not transcribed, because no inducer is present
Transcribed only if galactose is added
Transcribed, but only the z gene is expressed
questions.explanation:
The lac operon is under negative regulation. It stays off only when the repressor (the i gene product) binds the operator.
With the i gene deleted, no repressor is made, so the operator is always free.
RNA polymerase therefore transcribes the polycistronic z-y-a unit continuously, even with no lactose or inducer. This is constitutive expression.
Option (1) fails because an inducer is needed only to remove a repressor, and here there is none.
Option (2) fails because galactose is not an inducer.
Option (4) fails because z, y and a form one transcriptional unit, so all three are expressed together.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the approximate size of the genome of Escherichia coli?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives the E. coli genome as about $4.6 \times 10^{6}$ bp.
The other options are sizes of different genomes:
(1) 5386 nucleotides belongs to bacteriophage $\phi$X174.
(2) 48502 bp belongs to bacteriophage lambda.
(4) $3.3 \times 10^{9}$ bp is the haploid human genome.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A double-stranded DNA segment is 1000 bp long, and 30 per cent of its bases are adenine. How many hydrogen bonds hold its two strands together?
questions.explanation:
Given: 1000 bp, which is 2000 bases, with A = 30%.
Base pairing: A = T = 30% of 2000 = 600. G = C = 20% of 2000 = 400.
Pairs: 600 A–T pairs (2 H-bonds each) and 400 G–C pairs (3 H-bonds each).
Total: $600\times2 + 400\times3 = 1200 + 1200 = 2400$ hydrogen bonds.
Common slip: taking 30% of the 1000 bp as A–T pairs gives 2700, which is not even an option.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In prokaryotes, the predominant site for the control of gene expression is:
options: Transport of mRNA from nucleus to cytoplasm
questions.explanation:
In prokaryotes, the main point of control of gene expression is the rate of transcriptional initiation.
Prokaryotes have no nucleus and no split genes.
So splicing, nucleus-to-cytoplasm transport of mRNA, and capping and tailing do not happen in them. These are eukaryotic steps.
This leaves transcriptional initiation as the correct choice.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The distance between the two polynucleotide strands of the DNA double helix remains approximately uniform along its length.
Reason (R): In each base pair, a purine on one strand always lies opposite a pyrimidine on the other strand.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The two strands of the helix stay at a nearly constant distance from each other along the whole length.
R is true. Every base pair is a purine matched with a pyrimidine: A with T and G with C.
R explains A. A two-ring purine plus a one-ring pyrimidine gives every pair about the same width.
If two purines paired, the gap would be too wide. If two pyrimidines paired, it would be too narrow.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Southern blot hybridisation for DNA fingerprinting, the DNA fragments separated by electrophoresis are transferred (blotted) onto:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: After electrophoresis, the DNA fragments are transferred (blotted) from the gel onto synthetic membranes such as nitrocellulose or nylon.
The membrane holds the fragments in place so they can be hybridised with a labelled probe.
Why not agarose/polyacrylamide: these form the gel matrix in which the fragments are separated. They are not the blotting membrane.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (lac operon gene) with List-II (product):
List-I
(A) i gene
(B) z gene
(C) y gene
(D) a gene
List-II
(I) Transacetylase
(II) Permease
(III) Repressor
(IV) Beta-galactosidase
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
The correct pairs are:
(A) i gene → repressor (III)
(B) z gene → $\beta$-galactosidase (IV)
(C) y gene → permease (II)
(D) a gene → transacetylase (I)
Tip: remember the order 'z-y-a' as $\beta$-galactosidase, permease, transacetylase. Do not swap the y and z products.
This gives A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
A. Meselson and Stahl (1958)
B. Taylor and colleagues (1958)
C. Watson and Crick (1953)
D. DNA ligase
List-II:
I. Joins discontinuously synthesised fragments
II. Radioactive thymidine used in chromosomes of Vicia faba
III. $^{15}NH_4Cl$ and CsCl gradient used with E. coli
IV. First proposed the semiconservative scheme based on specific base pairing
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A – III: Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in $^{15}NH_4Cl$ and separated DNA by CsCl density gradient centrifugation.
B – II: Taylor and colleagues used radioactive thymidine on Vicia faba (faba bean) chromosomes. This showed that chromosomal DNA also replicates semiconservatively.
C – IV: Watson and Crick proposed the semiconservative replication scheme from specific base pairing.
D – I: DNA ligase joins the discontinuously synthesised fragments.
A common error is swapping the two 1958 experiments, as in option (2).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A nucleoside such as deoxyadenosine is formed when the nitrogenous base is joined to the pentose sugar. Which carbon of the sugar, and which type of bond, is involved?
questions.explanation:
A nitrogenous base joins to the OH group on the 1' C of the pentose sugar.
This bond is called an N-glycosidic linkage, and the product is a nucleoside, for example deoxyadenosine.
Option (1) is the common trap. The phosphoester linkage at 5' C adds a phosphate, which turns a nucleoside into a nucleotide.
A 3'–5' phosphodiester linkage joins neighbouring nucleotides into a chain. Hydrogen bonds join bases on opposite strands.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty is correct?
options: Treatment with protease abolished transformation, showing that the transforming principle is a protein
They used radioactive bacteriophages to identify the transforming principle
Treatment with RNase did not prevent transformation, which ruled out RNA as the transforming substance
Before their work, DNA was already widely accepted as the genetic material
questions.explanation:
Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified biochemicals from heat-killed S cells and tested them with enzymes.
Proteases and RNases did not stop transformation, so protein and RNA were ruled out. DNase did stop it, which pointed to DNA. So statement (3) is correct.
(1) is wrong: protease did not abolish transformation.
(2) is wrong: radioactive phages were used by Hershey and Chase.
(4) is wrong: before their work, protein was thought to be the genetic material.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia is a classic example of which type of mutation, and with what effect?
options: Frameshift deletion in the beta globin gene, changing all amino acids downstream
Point mutation in the alpha globin gene, changing valine to glutamate
Large deletion of the beta globin gene, causing loss of the beta chain
Change of a single base pair in the beta globin gene, replacing glutamate with valine
questions.explanation:
Key fact: sickle cell anaemia is caused by a single base-pair change (a point mutation) in the gene for the beta globin chain.
The effect is that glutamate (Glu) is replaced by valine (Val) in the beta chain.
Option (2) is a trap: it names the alpha chain and reverses the amino acids.
Options (1) and (3) describe frameshift and deletion mutations, which do not cause this disease.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In bacteria, translation of an mRNA can begin before its transcription is complete.
Reason (R): Bacterial mRNA needs no processing to become active, and bacteria have no separation between nucleus and cytosol.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In bacteria, transcription and translation are coupled, so ribosomes start translating an mRNA while it is still being transcribed.
R is true. Bacterial mRNA needs no splicing, capping or tailing to become functional.
R also explains A. Bacteria have no nuclear membrane, so transcription and translation happen in the same compartment, the cytosol. This lets translation begin immediately.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Heat-killed S strain bacteria alone, when injected, caused pneumonia and death in mice.
(ii) Griffith's experiment established that DNA is the genetic material.
(iii) Treatment with RNase did not affect transformation in the experiments of Avery and co-workers.
(iv) In the Hershey-Chase experiment, after infection with 32P-labelled phages, the radioactivity stayed mainly with the detached viral coats rather than in the bacteria.
(v) Griffith's observation that heat killed the bacteria but did not destroy the transforming ability indicates the stability of genetic material.
(vi) Before the work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, the genetic material was thought to be protein.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: heat-killed S cells injected alone did not harm the mice.
(ii) Incorrect: Griffith did not identify the biochemical nature of the transforming principle.
(iii) Correct: RNase did not affect transformation. Only DNase stopped it.
(iv) Incorrect: $^{32}P$-labelled DNA entered the cells, so the bacteria became radioactive.
(v) Correct: transforming ability survived heat, which shows the genetic material is stable.
(vi) Correct: before Avery's work, proteins were believed to carry genetic information.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the DNA fingerprinting technique originally developed by Alec Jeffreys, which of the following was used as the probe?
options: A radiolabelled VNTR, which is a mini-satellite DNA
A radiolabelled micro-satellite derived from coding DNA
A fluorescently labelled mRNA of a structural gene
A radiolabelled exon sequence of the beta globin gene
questions.explanation:
In Jeffreys' original technique, the probe was a radiolabelled VNTR. VNTR is a highly polymorphic satellite DNA, classed as a mini-satellite.
It was used in Southern blot hybridisation followed by autoradiography.
Option (2) fails because VNTR is a mini-satellite, not a micro-satellite, and it is non-coding.
Coding sequences, mRNAs and globin exons vary too little between people to give individual-specific patterns.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Viruses having an RNA genome mutate and evolve faster.
Reason (R): RNA is chemically more stable than DNA because of the 2'-OH group in its ribose.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. RNA viruses such as influenza and HIV mutate and evolve faster than DNA viruses.
R is false. The 2'-OH group on ribose is reactive. It makes RNA labile and easily degraded, so RNA is less stable than DNA, not more.
The correct explanation for A is this instability of RNA. NCERT also notes that RNA's catalytic, reactive nature contributes to faster mutation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bacterial RNA polymerase by itself can catalyse only elongation. It associates transiently with which factor to start transcription?
questions.explanation:
Bacterial RNA polymerase alone can only elongate an RNA chain.
To initiate transcription, it associates transiently with the $\sigma$ (sigma) factor, which lets it recognise and bind the promoter.
The tempting option, $\rho$ factor, works in termination, not initiation.
Release factor and initiator tRNA belong to translation, not transcription.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the lac operon of E. coli is correct?
options: The letter 'i' in the i gene refers to the inducer, lactose
The repressor protein is synthesised only when lactose is absent from the medium
Glucose and galactose can act as inducers of the lac operon
The inducer inactivates the repressor, allowing RNA polymerase access to the promoter
questions.explanation:
In the lac operon, the inducer (allolactose or lactose) binds the repressor and inactivates it. The operator becomes free, RNA polymerase can transcribe from the promoter, and statement (4) is correct.
(1) is wrong because 'i' stands for inhibitor, not inducer.
(2) is wrong because the repressor is made constitutively, whether or not lactose is present.
(3) is wrong because glucose and galactose do not act as inducers.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Ch 5 · Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Colonies of the S strain of Streptococcus pneumoniae appear smooth and shiny, unlike the rough colonies of the R strain. This is because S strain bacteria possess:
options: a mucous coat made of polysaccharide
a lipid-rich outer membrane absent in R strain
flagella that spread the colony evenly
questions.explanation:
According to NCERT, S strain cells have a mucous coat made of polysaccharide. This coat gives their colonies a smooth, shiny look.
The coat is also linked to virulence. R strain cells lack it, so they form rough colonies and do not cause pneumonia.
A 'protein capsid' belongs to viruses, not to bacteria, so option (2) is wrong.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a Meselson–Stahl type experiment, E. coli grown for many generations in $^{15}NH_4Cl$ is shifted to $^{14}NH_4Cl$ medium. E. coli divides every 20 minutes. What will be the ratio of light ($^{14}N/^{14}N$) to hybrid ($^{15}N/^{14}N$) DNA molecules after 60 minutes?
questions.explanation:
Given: DNA is fully $^{15}N$ at the start, and one generation takes 20 min. So 60 min = 3 generations.
One parent molecule gives $2^3 = 8$ DNA molecules.
Replication is semiconservative, so the two original $^{15}N$ strands stay intact and end up in 2 molecules. These 2 are hybrid ($^{15}N/^{14}N$).
The remaining 6 molecules are light ($^{14}N/^{14}N$). No heavy DNA remains.
So light : hybrid = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Match List-I (organism or genome) with List-II (genome size):
List-I
(a) Bacteriophage $\phi$X174
(b) Bacteriophage lambda
(c) Escherichia coli
(d) Human (haploid)
List-II
(i) $4.6 \times 10^{6}$ bp
(ii) 5386 nucleotides
(iii) $3.3 \times 10^{9}$ bp
(iv) 48502 bp
questions.explanation:
(a) $\phi$X174 has 5386 nucleotides, so a matches (ii). The size is given in nucleotides because its genome is single-stranded.
(b) Lambda phage has 48502 bp, so b matches (iv).
(c) E. coli has $4.6 \times 10^{6}$ bp, so c matches (i).
(d) The haploid human genome has $3.3 \times 10^{9}$ bp, so d matches (iii).
The correct pairing is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: In a Meselson–Stahl type experiment, E. coli with fully 15N-labelled DNA is transferred to a 14N medium. E. coli divides every 20 minutes. What will be the ratio of hybrid (15N/14N) DNA to light (14N/14N) DNA molecules after 80 minutes?
questions.explanation:
Given: all DNA starts as $^{15}N/^{15}N$. E. coli divides every 20 min, so 80 min = 4 generations.
Total DNA molecules after 4 generations = $2^4 = 16$.
Replication is semiconservative, so the 2 original $^{15}N$ strands are never lost. They end up in 2 hybrid ($^{15}N/^{14}N$) molecules.
Light ($^{14}N/^{14}N$) molecules = $16 - 2 = 14$.
So hybrid : light = 2 : 14 = 1 : 7. The ratio 1 : 3 (2 : 6) would apply after only 3 generations (60 min).
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. RNA polymerase I
B. RNA polymerase II
C. RNA polymerase III
D. $\sigma$ factor
List-II
i. hnRNA
ii. 28S, 18S and 5.8S rRNA
iii. tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA
iv. Initiation of transcription in bacteria
questions.explanation:
A. RNA pol I transcribes the large rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), so A-ii.
B. RNA pol II transcribes hnRNA, the precursor of mRNA, so B-i.
C. RNA pol III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA, so C-iii.
D. The $\sigma$ factor helps bacterial RNA polymerase start transcription, so D-iv.
A common trap is giving 5S rRNA to pol I. It is made by pol III.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Take the human genome as $3 \times 10^9$ bp, with 99.9 per cent of the bases identical among all humans. Approximately how many base positions would differ between two individuals?
questions.explanation:
Given: genome = $3 \times 10^9$ bp, and 99.9% of bases are identical.
So the differing fraction is $100 - 99.9 = 0.1\% = 0.001$.
Substituting: $0.001 \times 3 \times 10^9 = 3 \times 10^6$.
So about $3 \times 10^6$ base positions (3 million bp) differ between two people.
Common slip: taking 0.1% as 0.01 gives $3 \times 10^7$.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: During the Human Genome Project, random DNA fragments were cloned using specialised vectors called BAC and YAC. Which hosts were commonly used for this cloning?
questions.explanation:
In the HGP, total DNA was broken into random fragments that were cloned in suitable hosts using specialised vectors.
BAC stands for bacterial artificial chromosome, whose host is bacteria.
YAC stands for yeast artificial chromosome, whose host is yeast.
The hosts were therefore bacteria and yeast.
Option (1) fails because viruses are not the hosts for these vectors.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the findings of the Human Genome Project are correct?
(a) Chromosome 1 has the largest number of genes (2968).
(b) The Y chromosome has the fewest genes (231).
(c) Less than 2 per cent of the genome codes for proteins.
(d) Functions are known for over 50 per cent of the discovered genes.
(e) About 1.4 million single-base differences (SNPs) have been identified.
(f) The total number of genes is estimated at about 80,000.
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: chromosome 1 has the most genes, 2968.
(b) Correct: the Y chromosome has the fewest genes, 231.
(c) Correct: less than 2% of the genome codes for proteins.
(d) Incorrect: functions are unknown for over 50% of the discovered genes.
(e) Correct: about 1.4 million SNPs have been located.
(f) Incorrect: the total is about 30,000 genes. The figure of 80,000 to 1,40,000 was only an earlier estimate.
So 4 statements are correct.
Answer: (4)

questions.question: In a structural gene, one nucleotide is inserted within codon 3, and one nucleotide is deleted within codon 6 of the same reading frame. Assuming no stop codon is created, which statement best describes the effect on the encoded polypeptide?
options: Only amino acids 3 and 6 are changed; all others remain the same
All amino acids from position 3 to the end of the polypeptide are changed
Amino acids in the region from codon 3 to codon 6 may be altered, but the reading frame and amino acids beyond codon 6 are restored
No amino acid changes because the net change in number of bases is zero
questions.explanation:
Inserting one base in codon 3 shifts the reading frame. Codons from that point onward are misread, so amino acids in this stretch may change.
Deleting one base in codon 6 shifts the frame back to the original. Codons after codon 6 are read correctly again.
Option (4) fails because zero net change does not stop the misreading between the two mutations.
Option (2) fails because the frame is restored after codon 6.
The same reasoning supports the triplet nature of codons.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: In a Meselson–Stahl type experiment, E. coli grown for many generations in $^{15}NH_4Cl$ is transferred to a $^{14}NH_4Cl$ medium. E. coli divides every 20 minutes. After 80 minutes, what is the ratio of hybrid-density DNA to light-density DNA?
questions.explanation:
Given: E. coli divides every 20 min, so 80 min = 4 generations in $^{14}N$ medium.
Formula: one heavy DNA molecule gives $2^n$ molecules after $n$ generations. The two original $^{15}N$ strands always end up in 2 hybrid molecules.
Substituting: $2^4 = 16$ molecules, of which 2 are hybrid and 14 are light.
So hybrid : light = 2 : 14 = 1 : 7.
The trap answer 1 : 15 comes from counting single strands (2 heavy out of 32) instead of double-stranded molecules.
Answer: (3)
